lines.text: When a publisher turns off its servers, the game you paid for goes with it.
Last Save is a game licence that outlives its publisher.
Players took this fight to the European Commission. Last Save lets a studio make the promise in code, and earn a royalty on every resale.
Each licence is an NFT on NEAR. Forty percent of every sale is locked, by contract, for the day the studio leaves.
The server key sits in an enclave. Only this contract, running this exact program, can open it. The contract has no keys of its own, and no way to delete it.
Any studio can do the same. The licence code lives on NEAR as one global contract, and a new game launches in a single transaction, born with no keys.
Now the studio shuts the server down without a word. A signed heartbeat wouldn't save it: the contract only counts players who are actually being served.
Anyone can ask the enclave to check. Three probes fail. The contract declares the studio gone, and the enclave releases the server.
Every holder decides, without paying gas: take their share back, or keep the game alive. New players fund it too.
A fan runs one command. The released build checks out against the hash the studio committed to on day one.
The same players sign back in with the same progress. The host is paid per player session, and each session is signed by the player.
Hosts can even be paid on Base. NEAR's MPC network signs for the contract, so no one holds that key.
That's Last Save, built on NEAR. Thank you.
